WI:SCI.ESS1.A.1.cc_advanced: I can predict where the sun or moon will be at a later time using patterns I observed.
WI:SCI.ESS1.A.1.cc_at_target: I can observe, describe, and predict patterns of movement of the sun, moon, and stars as seen from Earth.
WI:SCI.ESS1.A.1.cc_approaching: I can describe where the sun is in the morning and afternoon, with help.
WI:SCI.ESS1.A.1.cc_emerging: I can point to the sun and moon in pictures of day and night sky.

WI:SCI.ESS1.A.5.cc_advanced: I can use data on size and distance to explain why the sun looks brighter than other stars.
WI:SCI.ESS1.A.5.cc_at_target: I can explain that stars vary greatly in size and distance from Earth, which explains their relative brightness.
WI:SCI.ESS1.A.5.cc_approaching: I can say that the sun looks bright because it is close, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS1.A.5.cc_emerging: I can say that the sun is a star.

WI:SCI.ESS1.A.m.cc_advanced: I can use a scale model to explain our place in the Milky Way and the universe.
WI:SCI.ESS1.A.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that the solar system is part of the Milky Way, one of billions of galaxies.
WI:SCI.ESS1.A.m.cc_approaching: I can order solar system, galaxy, and universe by size, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS1.A.m.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth is part of the solar system.

WI:SCI.ESS1.A.h.cc_advanced: I can use light spectra data to infer a star's properties and explain how stars make elements.
WI:SCI.ESS1.A.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that light spectra reveal star characteristics, stars make elements by fusion, and astronomical data supports theories of the universe.
WI:SCI.ESS1.A.h.cc_approaching: I can describe how scientists use light from stars to learn about them, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS1.A.h.cc_emerging: I can say that stars produce light.

WI:SCI.ESS1.B.1.cc_advanced: I can use observations to predict how daylight hours change through the year.
WI:SCI.ESS1.B.1.cc_at_target: I can observe, describe, and predict seasonal patterns of sunrise and sunset.
WI:SCI.ESS1.B.1.cc_approaching: I can compare when the sun rises in two seasons, using a chart with help.
WI:SCI.ESS1.B.1.cc_emerging: I can say that it is light in the day and dark at night.

WI:SCI.ESS1.B.5.cc_advanced: I can explain several patterns, such as shadows, day length, and moon phases, using Earth's and the moon's motions.
WI:SCI.ESS1.B.5.cc_at_target: I can explain that Earth's orbit and rotation and the moon's orbit cause observable patterns.
WI:SCI.ESS1.B.5.cc_approaching: I can show with a model how Earth's spin causes day and night, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS1.B.5.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth spins and moves around the sun.

WI:SCI.ESS1.B.m.cc_advanced: I can use a solar system model to predict an eclipse or lunar phase and explain the role of gravity.
WI:SCI.ESS1.B.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that gravity holds the solar system together and that models explain eclipses, lunar phases, and seasons.
WI:SCI.ESS1.B.m.cc_approaching: I can use a model to show the cause of one pattern, such as moon phases, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS1.B.m.cc_emerging: I can name objects in the solar system.

WI:SCI.ESS1.B.h.cc_advanced: I can apply Kepler's laws and orbital changes to explain solar system formation and long-term climate cycles.
WI:SCI.ESS1.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that Kepler's laws describe orbits, space data supports solar system formation ideas, and orbital changes affect climate.
WI:SCI.ESS1.B.h.cc_approaching: I can describe an elliptical orbit and one of Kepler's laws, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS1.B.h.cc_emerging: I can say that planets orbit the sun.

WI:SCI.ESS1.C.2.cc_advanced: I can compare fast and slow Earth events and give evidence for how long each takes.
WI:SCI.ESS1.C.2.cc_at_target: I can explain that some events on Earth happen very quickly and others very slowly.
WI:SCI.ESS1.C.2.cc_approaching: I can sort events, such as earthquakes and erosion, into fast or slow, with help.
WI:SCI.ESS1.C.2.cc_emerging: I can say that some changes to land happen fast.

WI:SCI.ESS1.C.4.cc_advanced: I can use rock layers and fossils to put a series of events in order and explain my reasoning.
WI:SCI.ESS1.C.4.cc_at_target: I can explain that certain features on Earth can be used to order events in a landscape.
WI:SCI.ESS1.C.4.cc_approaching: I can say which rock layer formed first, with a diagram and support.
WI:SCI.ESS1.C.4.cc_emerging: I can notice layers in rocks.

WI:SCI.ESS1.C.m.cc_advanced: I can use rock strata and fossils to build a timeline of major events and justify the order.
WI:SCI.ESS1.C.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that rock strata and the fossil record are evidence for the order of major events in Earth's history.
WI:SCI.ESS1.C.m.cc_approaching: I can use rock layers to put events in order, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS1.C.m.cc_emerging: I can say that lower layers are usually older.

WI:SCI.ESS1.C.h.cc_advanced: I can combine rock record and meteorite evidence to explain Earth's early history and date formations.
WI:SCI.ESS1.C.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that the rock record and solar system objects give evidence of Earth's early history and the ages of formations.
WI:SCI.ESS1.C.h.cc_approaching: I can describe how scientists date rocks, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS1.C.h.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth is very old.

WI:SCI.ESS2.A.2.cc_advanced: I can design a model to show how wind or water changes land and explain how to slow it.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.2.cc_at_target: I can explain that wind and water change the shape of the land.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.2.cc_approaching: I can show how water moves sand in a tray, with help.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.2.cc_emerging: I can say that wind blows sand.

WI:SCI.ESS2.A.4.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how weathering and erosion shaped a real landscape and its living things.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.4.cc_at_target: I can explain that rainfall shapes land and affects living things, and that water, ice, wind, organisms, and gravity break and move rock and soil.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.4.cc_approaching: I can describe how water or wind breaks down rock, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.4.cc_emerging: I can say that rocks can break into small pieces.

WI:SCI.ESS2.A.5.cc_advanced: I can model how the four Earth systems interact in a real example, such as a sandstorm.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.5.cc_at_target: I can explain that the geosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, and hydrosphere interact.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.5.cc_approaching: I can name the four Earth systems and give one example of each, with a word bank.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.5.cc_emerging: I can name land, water, air, and living things.

WI:SCI.ESS2.A.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how energy from the sun and Earth's interior drives matter cycles and plate tectonics.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that energy flows and matter cycles in Earth's systems, powered by the sun and Earth's interior, and that plate tectonics results.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.m.cc_approaching: I can describe one Earth cycle and its energy source, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.m.cc_emerging: I can name the sun as a source of energy for Earth.

WI:SCI.ESS2.A.h.cc_advanced: I can analyze data to show a chain of feedback effects among Earth's systems.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that feedback effects exist within and among Earth's systems.
WI:SCI.ESS2.A.h.cc_approaching: I can describe one feedback effect, such as melting ice, with support.

WI:SCI.ESS2.B.2.cc_advanced: I can make a map of an area showing land and water features and explain what it shows.
WI:SCI.ESS2.B.2.cc_at_target: I can explain that maps show where things are and can show the shapes and kinds of land and water in an area.
WI:SCI.ESS2.B.2.cc_approaching: I can find land and water on a map, with help.
WI:SCI.ESS2.B.2.cc_emerging: I can point to water and land in a picture.

WI:SCI.ESS2.B.4.cc_advanced: I can analyze maps to explain patterns of mountains, earthquakes, and volcanoes.
WI:SCI.ESS2.B.4.cc_at_target: I can explain that Earth's features, earthquakes, and volcanoes occur in patterns that maps can show.
WI:SCI.ESS2.B.4.cc_approaching: I can find where earthquakes happen on a map and describe a pattern, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS2.B.4.cc_emerging: I can name mountains, volcanoes, and oceans on a map.

WI:SCI.ESS2.B.m.cc_advanced: I can use map evidence to explain how plate movement formed specific features.
WI:SCI.ESS2.B.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that plate tectonics explains rock movement and geologic history and that maps show evidence of plate movement.
WI:SCI.ESS2.B.m.cc_approaching: I can identify plate boundaries on a map, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS2.B.m.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth's crust is made of plates.

WI:SCI.ESS2.B.h.cc_advanced: I can explain how radioactive decay heats Earth's interior and drives mantle convection and plate motion.
WI:SCI.ESS2.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that radioactive decay in Earth's interior contributes to thermal convection in the mantle.
WI:SCI.ESS2.B.h.cc_approaching: I can draw convection currents in the mantle, with support.

WI:SCI.ESS2.C.2.cc_advanced: I can map where water is found in my area and in what forms.
WI:SCI.ESS2.C.2.cc_at_target: I can explain that water is found in many places and in different forms on Earth.
WI:SCI.ESS2.C.2.cc_approaching: I can name places where water is found, such as the sea, with help.
WI:SCI.ESS2.C.2.cc_emerging: I can say that water can be liquid or ice.

WI:SCI.ESS2.C.5.cc_advanced: I can graph Earth's water and explain why fresh water is precious in places like Qatar.
WI:SCI.ESS2.C.5.cc_at_target: I can explain that most of Earth's water is in the ocean and much fresh water is in glaciers or underground.
WI:SCI.ESS2.C.5.cc_approaching: I can read a chart showing salt water and fresh water amounts, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS2.C.5.cc_emerging: I can say that oceans have salt water.

WI:SCI.ESS2.C.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how sunlight, gravity, and density differences move water and shape landscapes.
WI:SCI.ESS2.C.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that water cycles among land, ocean, and air, driven by sunlight and gravity, and causes weathering and erosion.
WI:SCI.ESS2.C.m.cc_approaching: I can label the water cycle and describe how water causes erosion, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS2.C.m.cc_emerging: I can say that rain falls from clouds.

WI:SCI.ESS2.C.h.cc_advanced: I can investigate a property of water and explain its effect on Earth's processes.
WI:SCI.ESS2.C.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that water's unique chemical and physical properties greatly influence Earth's dynamics.
WI:SCI.ESS2.C.h.cc_approaching: I can name properties of water, such as expanding when it freezes, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS2.C.h.cc_emerging: I can say that water can be solid, liquid, or gas.

WI:SCI.ESS2.D.K.cc_advanced: I can record weather over time and describe patterns I find.
WI:SCI.ESS2.D.K.cc_at_target: I can describe weather as sunlight, wind, rain, and temperature at a place and time and record it over time.
WI:SCI.ESS2.D.K.cc_approaching: I can record today's weather with symbols, with help.
WI:SCI.ESS2.D.K.cc_emerging: I can say if it is sunny or rainy.

WI:SCI.ESS2.D.3.cc_advanced: I can analyze weather data from two places and explain differences in their climates.
WI:SCI.ESS2.D.3.cc_at_target: I can explain that climate describes patterns of typical weather and that past weather patterns can be analyzed.
WI:SCI.ESS2.D.3.cc_approaching: I can read a weather table for a season and describe the typical weather, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS2.D.3.cc_emerging: I can say what the weather is usually like in summer.

WI:SCI.ESS2.D.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how ocean and air interactions create local weather and climate in a region.
WI:SCI.ESS2.D.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that complex interactions, including the ocean, determine local weather and influence climate.
WI:SCI.ESS2.D.m.cc_approaching: I can describe how the sea affects weather near the coast, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS2.D.m.cc_emerging: I can tell the difference between weather and climate, with help.

WI:SCI.ESS2.D.h.cc_advanced: I can use climate model results to explain how human and natural factors change global climate.
WI:SCI.ESS2.D.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that solar radiation and its interactions form the climate system and that models predict future change.
WI:SCI.ESS2.D.h.cc_approaching: I can describe the greenhouse effect using a diagram, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS2.D.h.cc_emerging: I can say that the sun warms Earth.

WI:SCI.ESS2.E.K.cc_advanced: I can give several examples of how plants and animals change their environment and explain why.
WI:SCI.ESS2.E.K.cc_at_target: I can explain that plants and animals can change their local environment.
WI:SCI.ESS2.E.K.cc_approaching: I can give one example, such as a bird building a nest, with help.
WI:SCI.ESS2.E.K.cc_emerging: I can say that animals dig holes or build homes.

WI:SCI.ESS2.E.4.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how living things changed the physical features of a place.
WI:SCI.ESS2.E.4.cc_at_target: I can explain that living things can affect the physical characteristics of their environment.
WI:SCI.ESS2.E.4.cc_approaching: I can describe how plant roots can break rocks, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS2.E.4.cc_emerging: I can say that animals change the places they live.

WI:SCI.ESS2.E.m.cc_advanced: I can use fossil evidence to describe how life and environments changed over Earth's history.
WI:SCI.ESS2.E.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that the fossil record documents the existence, diversity, extinction, and change of life forms through history.
WI:SCI.ESS2.E.m.cc_approaching: I can describe what fossils tell us about past life, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS2.E.m.cc_emerging: I can say that fossils are evidence of past life.

WI:SCI.ESS2.E.h.cc_advanced: I can argue with evidence how life and Earth's surface have changed each other over time.
WI:SCI.ESS2.E.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that the biosphere and Earth's other systems are interconnected and have coevolved over time.
WI:SCI.ESS2.E.h.cc_approaching: I can give one example of life changing Earth's systems, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS2.E.h.cc_emerging: I can say that living things affect air, water, and land.

WI:SCI.ESS3.A.K.cc_advanced: I can explain how different animals' homes give them what they need and how people use natural resources.
WI:SCI.ESS3.A.K.cc_at_target: I can explain that living things need water, air, and land resources, live where they can get them, and that humans use natural resources.
WI:SCI.ESS3.A.K.cc_approaching: I can match an animal to the place it lives and what it needs, with help.
WI:SCI.ESS3.A.K.cc_emerging: I can say that animals need water and food.

WI:SCI.ESS3.A.4.cc_advanced: I can compare renewable and nonrenewable energy sources and explain their effects on the environment.
WI:SCI.ESS3.A.4.cc_at_target: I can explain that energy and fuels come from natural sources, their use affects the environment, and some are renewable.
WI:SCI.ESS3.A.4.cc_approaching: I can sort energy sources into renewable and nonrenewable, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS3.A.4.cc_emerging: I can name energy sources, such as the sun and oil.

WI:SCI.ESS3.A.m.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence why resources are unevenly distributed and how this affects people.
WI:SCI.ESS3.A.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that humans depend on limited Earth resources that are unevenly distributed because of past geologic processes.
WI:SCI.ESS3.A.m.cc_approaching: I can describe where a resource is found and why it is limited, with support.

WI:SCI.ESS3.A.h.cc_advanced: I can analyze how a resource shaped a society, such as natural gas in Qatar, and weigh its costs and benefits.
WI:SCI.ESS3.A.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that resource availability has guided human society and that using resources has costs, risks, and benefits.
WI:SCI.ESS3.A.h.cc_approaching: I can list a cost and a benefit of using a natural resource, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS3.A.h.cc_emerging: I can name resources people use.

WI:SCI.ESS3.B.K.cc_advanced: I can explain how forecasts help my community prepare for the severe weather common in our region.
WI:SCI.ESS3.B.K.cc_at_target: I can explain that some severe weather is more likely in a region and that forecasts help communities prepare.
WI:SCI.ESS3.B.K.cc_approaching: I can name a type of severe weather and one way to stay safe, with help.
WI:SCI.ESS3.B.K.cc_emerging: I can name types of weather, such as storms.

WI:SCI.ESS3.B.3,4.cc_advanced: I can compare solutions that reduce the impact of a natural hazard and choose the best with reasons.
WI:SCI.ESS3.B.3,4.cc_at_target: I can explain that natural processes cause hazards that humans cannot stop but can reduce their impacts.
WI:SCI.ESS3.B.3,4.cc_approaching: I can name a natural hazard and one way people reduce its harm, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS3.B.3,4.cc_emerging: I can name natural hazards, such as floods.

WI:SCI.ESS3.B.m.cc_advanced: I can analyze hazard maps and geologic data to forecast risk in a region.
WI:SCI.ESS3.B.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that mapping the history of natural hazards and understanding geologic forces reveals patterns.
WI:SCI.ESS3.B.m.cc_approaching: I can describe a pattern on a hazard map, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS3.B.m.cc_emerging: I can name places where earthquakes happen, using a map.

WI:SCI.ESS3.B.h.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence how a natural hazard changed the history of a community or region.
WI:SCI.ESS3.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that natural hazards and geologic events have shaped human history at local, regional, and global scales.
WI:SCI.ESS3.B.h.cc_approaching: I can describe how one natural hazard affected people, with a case study and support.

WI:SCI.ESS3.C.K.cc_advanced: I can suggest several ways people can reduce their impact and explain how each helps.
WI:SCI.ESS3.C.K.cc_at_target: I can explain that things people do affect the environment and that people can make choices to reduce their impact.
WI:SCI.ESS3.C.K.cc_approaching: I can name one way to help the environment, such as recycling, with help.
WI:SCI.ESS3.C.K.cc_emerging: I can say that litter is bad for the environment.

WI:SCI.ESS3.C.5.cc_advanced: I can research how a community protects resources and evaluate how well it works.
WI:SCI.ESS3.C.5.cc_at_target: I can explain that human activities have affected land, ocean, air, and space and can also protect Earth's resources.
WI:SCI.ESS3.C.5.cc_approaching: I can describe one human effect on the environment and one way to protect it, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS3.C.5.cc_emerging: I can name ways people protect nature.

WI:SCI.ESS3.C.m.cc_advanced: I can trace how a human activity changes one sphere and then the biosphere, and propose a technology to reduce it.
WI:SCI.ESS3.C.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that human activities have altered Earth's spheres and biosphere and that technologies can be engineered to reduce impacts.
WI:SCI.ESS3.C.m.cc_approaching: I can describe how a human activity changes air, water, or land, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS3.C.m.cc_emerging: I can name ways people change the environment.

WI:SCI.ESS3.C.h.cc_advanced: I can evaluate a resource management plan and technology for sustaining people and biodiversity.
WI:SCI.ESS3.C.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that sustaining societies and biodiversity requires responsible resource management, including new technologies.
WI:SCI.ESS3.C.h.cc_approaching: I can describe one sustainable practice and why it matters, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS3.C.h.cc_emerging: I can say what sustainability means, with an example.

WI:SCI.ESS3.D.m.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence that human activities cause warming and propose solutions considering science, engineering, and society.
WI:SCI.ESS3.D.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that evidence shows human activities affect global warming and that solutions depend on science, engineering, and social factors.
WI:SCI.ESS3.D.m.cc_approaching: I can name a human activity that causes warming and one solution, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS3.D.m.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth is getting warmer.

WI:SCI.ESS3.D.h.cc_advanced: I can evaluate the strengths and limits of climate models and explain how new evidence improves them.
WI:SCI.ESS3.D.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that global climate models used to predict change keep improving as discoveries continue.
WI:SCI.ESS3.D.h.cc_approaching: I can describe what a climate model predicts, with support.
WI:SCI.ESS3.D.h.cc_emerging: I can say that scientists use models to predict climate.

WI:SCI.ETS1.A.K-2.cc_advanced: I can ask questions and gather information to clearly define a problem before designing.
WI:SCI.ETS1.A.K-2.cc_at_target: I can explain that a situation people want to change can be a problem to solve and that asking questions and observing help define it.
WI:SCI.ETS1.A.K-2.cc_approaching: I can describe a problem I want to solve, with help.
WI:SCI.ETS1.A.K-2.cc_emerging: I can say something that needs fixing.

WI:SCI.ETS1.A.3-5.cc_advanced: I can define criteria and constraints and compare proposals using them.
WI:SCI.ETS1.A.3-5.cc_at_target: I can explain that solutions are limited by constraints, judged by criteria, and can be compared on how well they meet both.
WI:SCI.ETS1.A.3-5.cc_approaching: I can list one criterion and one constraint for a design, with a template.
WI:SCI.ETS1.A.3-5.cc_emerging: I can say what my design needs to do.

WI:SCI.ETS1.A.m.cc_advanced: I can precisely define criteria and constraints, including scientific limits, for a design task.
WI:SCI.ETS1.A.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that precisely defined criteria and constraints, including scientific principles, make a successful design more likely.
WI:SCI.ETS1.A.m.cc_approaching: I can write criteria and constraints for a design task, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS1.A.m.cc_emerging: I can describe a design problem.

WI:SCI.ETS1.A.h.cc_advanced: I can quantify criteria and constraints, including societal requirements and risk, for a global problem.
WI:SCI.ETS1.A.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that criteria and constraints include societal requirements and should be quantified so designs can be checked.
WI:SCI.ETS1.A.h.cc_approaching: I can write measurable criteria for a design, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS1.A.h.cc_emerging: I can list what a solution must do.

WI:SCI.ETS1.B.K-2.cc_advanced: I can communicate my design idea clearly with a labeled sketch and a model.
WI:SCI.ETS1.B.K-2.cc_at_target: I can explain that designs can be shared through sketches, drawings, or models.
WI:SCI.ETS1.B.K-2.cc_approaching: I can draw my design idea, with help.
WI:SCI.ETS1.B.K-2.cc_emerging: I can show my idea using blocks or a drawing.

WI:SCI.ETS1.B.3-5.cc_advanced: I can research a problem, test my solution under different conditions, and use peer feedback to improve it.
WI:SCI.ETS1.B.3-5.cc_at_target: I can explain that research comes before designing, testing checks performance under different conditions, and sharing ideas helps.
WI:SCI.ETS1.B.3-5.cc_approaching: I can test my design and share results with a partner, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS1.B.3-5.cc_emerging: I can test a design to see if it works.

WI:SCI.ETS1.B.m.cc_advanced: I can use a systematic process to test, evaluate, and combine the best parts of different designs.
WI:SCI.ETS1.B.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that solutions are tested and modified based on results and evaluated systematically against criteria and constraints.
WI:SCI.ETS1.B.m.cc_approaching: I can test a design, record results, and make one change, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS1.B.m.cc_emerging: I can test a design and say if it worked.

WI:SCI.ETS1.B.h.cc_advanced: I can evaluate solutions using cost, safety, reliability, aesthetics, and social and environmental impacts, using models or computers.
WI:SCI.ETS1.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that evaluating solutions requires considering many constraints and impacts and that physical and computer models help.
WI:SCI.ETS1.B.h.cc_approaching: I can evaluate a solution against two or three constraints, with a template.
WI:SCI.ETS1.B.h.cc_emerging: I can list good and bad points of a solution.

WI:SCI.ETS1.C.K-2.cc_advanced: I can test two designs and explain which works better and why.
WI:SCI.ETS1.C.K-2.cc_at_target: I can explain that there is more than one solution to a problem, so it is useful to compare and test designs.
WI:SCI.ETS1.C.K-2.cc_approaching: I can compare two designs and say which I like, with help.
WI:SCI.ETS1.C.K-2.cc_emerging: I can try out a design.

WI:SCI.ETS1.C.3-5.cc_advanced: I can design a fair test to compare solutions and choose the best one using data.
WI:SCI.ETS1.C.3-5.cc_at_target: I can explain that different solutions must be tested to find which best solves the problem given criteria and constraints.
WI:SCI.ETS1.C.3-5.cc_approaching: I can test two solutions and compare results, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS1.C.3-5.cc_emerging: I can test a solution and record what happened.

WI:SCI.ETS1.C.m.cc_advanced: I can combine the best features of several tested designs into an improved design and justify it.
WI:SCI.ETS1.C.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that identifying the best-performing features of each design gives useful information for redesign.
WI:SCI.ETS1.C.m.cc_approaching: I can identify the best feature of a tested design, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS1.C.m.cc_emerging: I can say which part of a design worked best.

WI:SCI.ETS1.C.h.cc_advanced: I can break down criteria, prioritize them, and justify trade-offs in a complex design.
WI:SCI.ETS1.C.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that criteria may be broken into simpler ones and that trade-offs between criteria may be needed.
WI:SCI.ETS1.C.h.cc_approaching: I can rank criteria by importance, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS1.C.h.cc_emerging: I can list criteria for a design.

WI:SCI.ETS2.A.K-2.cc_advanced: I can explain how science ideas helped me design and share a solution.
WI:SCI.ETS2.A.K-2.cc_at_target: I can explain that designs can be shared through sketches, drawings, or physical models to communicate ideas.
WI:SCI.ETS2.A.K-2.cc_approaching: I can draw and explain my design to a partner, with help.

WI:SCI.ETS2.A.3-5.cc_advanced: I can research science ideas for a design and test it under several conditions.
WI:SCI.ETS2.A.3-5.cc_at_target: I can explain that research should come before designing and that testing checks how a solution performs.
WI:SCI.ETS2.A.3-5.cc_approaching: I can find information to help my design, with support.

WI:SCI.ETS2.A.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how science and engineering depend on each other using an example of a tested and improved design.
WI:SCI.ETS2.A.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that solutions are tested and modified based on results and evaluated systematically.
WI:SCI.ETS2.A.m.cc_approaching: I can describe how test results helped improve a design, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS2.A.m.cc_emerging: I can say that engineers test and improve designs.

WI:SCI.ETS2.A.h.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how science, engineering, and technology together address a complex problem, including its constraints and impacts.
WI:SCI.ETS2.A.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that evaluating solutions requires considering cost, safety, reliability, aesthetics, and social, cultural, and environmental impacts.
WI:SCI.ETS2.A.h.cc_approaching: I can evaluate a solution against some constraints, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS2.A.h.cc_emerging: I can name constraints such as cost and safety.

WI:SCI.ETS2.B.K-2.cc_advanced: I can explain how a product is made from natural materials and how this affects the environment.
WI:SCI.ETS2.B.K-2.cc_at_target: I can explain that products are designed using knowledge of nature, built from natural materials, and that taking materials affects the environment.
WI:SCI.ETS2.B.K-2.cc_approaching: I can name the natural material an object is made from, with help.
WI:SCI.ETS2.B.K-2.cc_emerging: I can say that paper comes from trees.

WI:SCI.ETS2.B.3-5.cc_advanced: I can explain how a technology has changed over time to meet people's needs and reduce risks.
WI:SCI.ETS2.B.3-5.cc_at_target: I can explain that needs change, engineers improve technologies to increase benefits and reduce risks, and new technologies affect society.
WI:SCI.ETS2.B.3-5.cc_approaching: I can compare an old and new technology, such as phones, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS2.B.3-5.cc_emerging: I can name technologies I use.

WI:SCI.ETS2.B.m.cc_advanced: I can analyze the short and long-term effects of a technology on people and the environment.
WI:SCI.ETS2.B.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that technologies use natural resources, have positive and negative effects, and are driven by people's needs and values.
WI:SCI.ETS2.B.m.cc_approaching: I can list one positive and one negative effect of a technology, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS2.B.m.cc_emerging: I can name a technology and what it is used for.

WI:SCI.ETS2.B.h.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how engineers modify a major technological system, such as water or energy, to balance benefits and risks.
WI:SCI.ETS2.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that society depends on major technological systems that engineers modify to increase benefits and reduce costs and risks.
WI:SCI.ETS2.B.h.cc_approaching: I can describe a technological system, such as water supply, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS2.B.h.cc_emerging: I can name systems people depend on, such as electricity.

WI:SCI.ETS3.A.K-2.cc_advanced: I can tell about scientists and engineers from different backgrounds and how they used creativity.
WI:SCI.ETS3.A.K-2.cc_at_target: I can explain that people of diverse backgrounds become scientists and engineers and that creativity and imagination are important.
WI:SCI.ETS3.A.K-2.cc_approaching: I can name a scientist or engineer and what they do, with help.
WI:SCI.ETS3.A.K-2.cc_emerging: I can say that anyone can be a scientist.

WI:SCI.ETS3.A.3-5.cc_advanced: I can explain how science knowledge from different cultures, including Arab scientists, has helped people.
WI:SCI.ETS3.A.3-5.cc_at_target: I can explain that many cultures created science knowledge and that many jobs use science and engineering in daily life.
WI:SCI.ETS3.A.3-5.cc_approaching: I can name a job that uses science, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS3.A.3-5.cc_emerging: I can name people who use science at work.

WI:SCI.ETS3.A.m.cc_advanced: I can research contributions from different cultures and explain the traits that made those scientists successful.
WI:SCI.ETS3.A.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that people from many cultures contributed to science and that scientists use creativity, reasoning, and skepticism.
WI:SCI.ETS3.A.m.cc_approaching: I can describe a contribution from a scientist of another culture, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS3.A.m.cc_emerging: I can name a famous scientist.

WI:SCI.ETS3.A.h.cc_advanced: I can analyze how a scientist's background shaped their questions and how peer critique improved the work.
WI:SCI.ETS3.A.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that diverse backgrounds bring valuable perspectives and influence the questions scientists and engineers ask.
WI:SCI.ETS3.A.h.cc_approaching: I can describe how a scientist's background influenced their work, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS3.A.h.cc_emerging: I can say that scientists come from many backgrounds.

WI:SCI.ETS3.B.K-2.cc_advanced: I can explain the difference between what scientists do and what engineers do with examples.
WI:SCI.ETS3.B.K-2.cc_at_target: I can explain that scientists use evidence to explain the natural world and engineers solve problems for people.
WI:SCI.ETS3.B.K-2.cc_approaching: I can say what a scientist or engineer does, with help.
WI:SCI.ETS3.B.K-2.cc_emerging: I can say that scientists study nature.

WI:SCI.ETS3.B.3-5.cc_advanced: I can explain how a scientific finding is supported by evidence and why laws of nature are the same everywhere.
WI:SCI.ETS3.B.3-5.cc_at_target: I can explain that science and engineering are knowledge and processes, that findings need evidence, and that natural laws apply everywhere.
WI:SCI.ETS3.B.3-5.cc_approaching: I can explain why scientists need evidence, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS3.B.3-5.cc_emerging: I can say that scientists collect evidence.

WI:SCI.ETS3.B.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how scientists handle unexpected data and why some questions cannot be answered by science.
WI:SCI.ETS3.B.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that science assumes consistent natural patterns, uses measurement and observation, and carefully evaluates anomalies in data.
WI:SCI.ETS3.B.m.cc_approaching: I can describe what scientists do with surprising results, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS3.B.m.cc_emerging: I can say that science asks questions about nature.

WI:SCI.ETS3.B.h.cc_advanced: I can explain how a scientific idea changed over history and what makes science different from other ways of knowing.
WI:SCI.ETS3.B.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that science is both knowledge and processes for revising it and that these processes set science apart from other ways of knowing.
WI:SCI.ETS3.B.h.cc_approaching: I can describe how one scientific idea changed over time, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS3.B.h.cc_emerging: I can say that science knowledge can change with new evidence.

WI:SCI.ETS3.C.K-2.cc_advanced: I can give examples of different ways to answer a question and different solutions to one problem.
WI:SCI.ETS3.C.K-2.cc_at_target: I can explain that scientists and engineers use many approaches, explanations need evidence, and a problem can have many solutions.
WI:SCI.ETS3.C.K-2.cc_approaching: I can name two ways to find out about something, with help.
WI:SCI.ETS3.C.K-2.cc_emerging: I can say that there is more than one way to solve a problem.

WI:SCI.ETS3.C.3-5.cc_advanced: I can compare the approaches used in two investigations and explain why both are scientific.
WI:SCI.ETS3.C.3-5.cc_at_target: I can explain that science and engineering do not follow one fixed method but use many practices, and explanations rest on evidence.
WI:SCI.ETS3.C.3-5.cc_approaching: I can describe two different ways scientists investigate, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS3.C.3-5.cc_emerging: I can name one way scientists investigate.

WI:SCI.ETS3.C.m.cc_advanced: I can explain how peer review tested a scientific theory and made it stronger.
WI:SCI.ETS3.C.m.cc_at_target: I can explain that a theory explains part of the natural world, is developed with many approaches, and is strengthened by peer review.
WI:SCI.ETS3.C.m.cc_approaching: I can explain the difference between a theory and a guess, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS3.C.m.cc_emerging: I can say what a scientific theory is, with help.

WI:SCI.ETS3.C.h.cc_advanced: I can evaluate the evidence for a scientific theory and explain how multiple methods confirmed it.
WI:SCI.ETS3.C.h.cc_at_target: I can explain that scientists use many methods to develop theories, which are explanations based on repeatedly confirmed evidence.
WI:SCI.ETS3.C.h.cc_approaching: I can describe the evidence for one theory, with support.
WI:SCI.ETS3.C.h.cc_emerging: I can name a scientific theory.

WI:K-ETS3-1.cc_advanced: I can compare results from a hands-on test and a computer game and explain what both show about pushes and pulls.
WI:K-ETS3-1.cc_at_target: I can compare data from two types of investigations to show that pushes and pulls of different strengths have different effects.
WI:K-ETS3-1.cc_approaching: I can tell what happened with a strong and weak push in one investigation, with help.
WI:K-ETS3-1.cc_emerging: I can push a toy softly and strongly.

WI:1-ETS3-1.cc_advanced: I can give several examples of people using ideas from plants and animals to survive, now and long ago.
WI:1-ETS3-1.cc_at_target: I can construct an argument with evidence that humans today and long ago used ideas from plants and animals to survive.
WI:1-ETS3-1.cc_approaching: I can give one example of a tool that copies an animal or plant, with help.
WI:1-ETS3-1.cc_emerging: I can name animal parts, such as claws or shells.

WI:2-ETS3-1.cc_advanced: I can design and test creative solutions to protect people from a quick change to Earth's surface.
WI:2-ETS3-1.cc_at_target: I can design creative solutions to a problem caused by a quick change to Earth's surface, such as a natural disaster.
WI:2-ETS3-1.cc_approaching: I can suggest one way to protect a house from a flood, with help.
WI:2-ETS3-1.cc_emerging: I can name a natural disaster.

WI:3-ETS3-1.cc_advanced: I can compare tools from different cultures and explain how each helps people survive in its environment.
WI:3-ETS3-1.cc_at_target: I can obtain and evaluate information showing that different cultures created different tools to survive in different environments.
WI:3-ETS3-1.cc_approaching: I can describe one tool people use to survive in the desert, with support.
WI:3-ETS3-1.cc_emerging: I can name tools people use.

WI:4-ETS3-1.cc_advanced: I can explain energy transfer in a system and revise my explanation when I get new evidence.
WI:4-ETS3-1.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation for how energy is transferred in a system and revise it based on new evidence.
WI:4-ETS3-1.cc_approaching: I can describe one energy transfer in a system, with support.
WI:4-ETS3-1.cc_emerging: I can say that energy can move from place to place.

WI:5-ETS3-1.cc_advanced: I can test properties of several materials and justify which is best for my design.
WI:5-ETS3-1.cc_at_target: I can investigate properties of materials to show which would work best in an engineering design solution.
WI:5-ETS3-1.cc_approaching: I can test one property of materials, such as strength, with support.
WI:5-ETS3-1.cc_emerging: I can describe materials as hard or soft.

WI:MS-ETS3-1.cc_advanced: I can argue with evidence how different societies' values show in what they spend on space exploration.
WI:MS-ETS3-1.cc_at_target: I can construct an argument with evidence about the values of different societies based on resources spent exploring the universe.
WI:MS-ETS3-1.cc_approaching: I can describe what one country does in space exploration, with support.
WI:MS-ETS3-1.cc_emerging: I can name a space mission.

WI:MS-ETS3-2.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence about genetically modified organisms and sort questions science can and cannot answer.
WI:MS-ETS3-2.cc_at_target: I can evaluate information about genetically modifying organisms and identify questions that can and cannot be answered by science.
WI:MS-ETS3-2.cc_approaching: I can describe one benefit and one concern about GMOs, with support.
WI:MS-ETS3-2.cc_emerging: I can say what a genetically modified plant is, with help.

WI:MS-ETS3-3.cc_advanced: I can use mass data from several changes to show how they support atomic theory.
WI:MS-ETS3-3.cc_at_target: I can mathematically evaluate products of chemical and physical changes to support atomic theory.
WI:MS-ETS3-3.cc_approaching: I can compare mass before and after a change, with support.
WI:MS-ETS3-3.cc_emerging: I can measure mass with a balance.

WI:HS-ETS3-1.cc_advanced: I can analyze why an author spreads false science information and evaluate the evidence against it.
WI:HS-ETS3-1.cc_at_target: I can ask questions to clarify an author's motivation for promoting unscientific or falsified information on science topics.
WI:HS-ETS3-1.cc_approaching: I can ask questions to check if a science article is reliable, with question stems.
WI:HS-ETS3-1.cc_emerging: I can say why some information online may be false.

WI:HS-ETS3-2.cc_advanced: I can build a simulation of antibiotic resistance and explain how ideas about antibiotic use changed over time.
WI:HS-ETS3-2.cc_at_target: I can create simulations showing how antibiotic use over time affected bacterial evolution and reflect on how views of antibiotic use changed.
WI:HS-ETS3-2.cc_approaching: I can explain how bacteria become resistant to antibiotics, with a diagram.
WI:HS-ETS3-2.cc_emerging: I can say what antibiotics are used for.

WI:HS-ETS3-3.cc_advanced: I can compare several approaches to studying climate change and explain how together they strengthen the theory.
WI:HS-ETS3-3.cc_at_target: I can provide evidence that multiple approaches to understanding climate change have made stronger theories of why change happens.
WI:HS-ETS3-3.cc_approaching: I can describe two ways scientists study climate change, with support.
WI:HS-ETS3-3.cc_emerging: I can say that scientists study climate.
